newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says bank loans to Victorias covered.
newsitem.headline: Manila says bank loans to Victorias covered.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Tuesday that sugar miller Victorias Milling Co has enough assets to pay for about 6.413 billion pesos in total bank loans.
Central Bank director Andres Rustia told Reuters in a telephone interview the Central Bank had evaluated all of the banks with exposure to the cash-strapped Victorias.
Of the total loan portfolio as of March 12, 3.466 billion pesos are secured by collateral and 2.947 billion pesos are unsecured, he said.
"The company has more assets than liabilities," Rustia said. "That should not be a source of serious concern on the part of creditors."
Victorias earlier this month obtained a 90-day moratorium on payments on the principal amount of its loans from 32 banks.
Meanwhile, creditors of Victorias said no legal action will be taken against Victorias despite a delay in the payment of interest fees by the sugar miller.

Some creditor banks said on Monday that they had yet to receive their portions of the interest payments because the bank nominated to accept the 110 million pesos payment had not transferred it to the other creditors.
Isidro Alcantara, chairman of the creditors committee, said on Tuesday that the memorandum of agreement on the 90-day moratorium will likely be signed within the week.

"We are confident that Victorias will be able to place the funds very soon," he said referring to the interest payments. He said the creditors did not plan to take legal action against the sugar miller over the delayed payment, but would rather work with the company on a rescue plan.
